sentences: Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for cutting concrete kerbs, blocks and paving with a cut-off saw, eliminate or limit the dust by limiting the number of cuts during design/layout, using lower energy equipment like block splitters, and getting material cut off site and delivered; control the dust by using water suppression and RPE* with an APF of 20.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for chasing concrete and raking mortar, eliminate or limit the dust by limiting the need for chasing at the design/layout stage and using a work method that limits/does not need chasing, like over-covering cables; control the dust by using on-tool extraction using an H or M Class extraction unit and RPE* with an APF of 20 – consider powered RPE for longer duration work.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for cutting roofing tiles with a cut-off saw, eliminate or limit the dust by hand cutting natural/fibre cement slates and other tiles where possible, using ½ and 1½ tiles, correct setting out/design, and minimising valleys/using dry valleys; control the dust by using water suppression, a dedicated cutting area with scaffold board protection, and RPE* with an APF of 20.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for scabbling or grinding with hand-held tools, eliminate or limit the dust by specifying architectural finishes that do not need scabbling, using (ultra) high-pressure water jetting, using chemical retarders and pressure washing, and casting in proprietary joint formers, eg mesh formwork; control the dust by where possible using on-tool extraction using an H or M Class extraction unit and RPE* with an APF of 20.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for occasional short-duration drilling with hand-held rotary power tools, eliminate or limit the dust by limiting the number of holes during design/planning and using direct fastening or screws; control the dust by where possible using equipment that stops dust getting into the air (the larger the holes the better this needs to be, with options ranging from drilling through a dust ‘collector’ or using cordless extraction attached to the drill (for smaller drill bits) or on-tool extraction using an H or M Class extraction unit), otherwise using RPE* with an APF of 20.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for drilling holes with hand-held rotary power tools as a ‘main activity’, eliminate or limit the dust by limiting the number of holes during design/planning and using direct fastening or screws; control the dust by where possible using on-tool extraction using an H or M Class extraction unit and RPE* with an APF of 20.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for dry coring, eliminate or limit the dust by limiting the number of holes during design/planning; control the dust by using on-tool extraction using an H or M Class extraction unit, and longer duration work will also need RPE.* Use an APF of 20.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for wet coring, eliminate or limit the dust by limiting the number of holes during design/planning; control the dust by using water suppression, and long periods of wet coring in enclosed spaces may also need RPE.* Use an APF of 20.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for using a hand-held breaker in enclosed spaces with limited ventilation, eliminate or limit the dust by limiting the amount of breaking during design/planning stage, bursting, crushing, cutting, sawing or other techniques, and remote controlled demolition; control the dust by using on-tool extraction using an H or M Class extraction unit and RPE* with an APF of 20.

Use water suppression or on-tool extraction for those tasks where it is possible and; RPE* with an APF of 20 – consider powered RPE for longer duration work; Enclosed spaces may also need general mechanical ventilation to remove dusty air

Damping down and using a brush, shovel and bucket for minor/small ‘one-off’ amounts; Or for regular removal/site cleaning: water spray for damping down; Rake, shovel and bucket/wheelbarrow to remove larger pieces; Covered chutes and skips where needed; Vacuum attachments fitted to an H or M Class extraction unit; RPE* with an APF of 20 depending upon location, duration and type of work

sentences: Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for abrasive pressure blasting, eliminate or limit the dust by using a different method of work like (ultra) high-pressure water jetting and using ‘silica free’ abrasive material; control the dust by using wet or vacuum blasting and RPE* that will depend on silica content of building materials, blasting equipment and length of work (in most instances use RPE with an APF of 40, and use RPE with an APF of 20 for lower risk work, including the ‘potman’ nearby), shrouds or screens to contain the flying abrasive, and note that certain restricted/enclosed working places may also need general mechanical ventilation.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for soft strip demolition, eliminate or limit the dust by carefully planning the work, limiting the number of people that need to be in the work area, and screening off areas to prevent dust spreading; control the dust by using water suppression or on-tool extraction for those tasks where it is possible and RPE* with an APF of 20 – consider powered RPE for longer duration work, and note that enclosed spaces may also need general mechanical ventilation to remove dusty air.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for removing small rubble, dust and debris, eliminate or limit the dust by limiting waste materials during design/planning, considering where waste material is created and how frequently it needs removing, and using the correct dust controls when making rubble/debris; control the dust by damping down and using a brush, shovel and bucket for minor/small ‘one-off’ amounts, or for regular removal/site cleaning by using water spray for damping down, rake, shovel and bucket/wheelbarrow to remove larger pieces, covered chutes and skips where needed, vacuum attachments fitted to an H or M Class extraction unit, and RPE* with an APF of 20 depending upon location, duration and type of work.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for cutting wood with power tools, eliminate or limit the dust by ordering pre-cut materials and using dedicated cutting areas to minimise spread; control the dust by using on-tool extraction using an H or M Class extraction unit and RPE* with an APF of 20 in most situations.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for sanding wood with power tools, eliminate or limit the dust by using ‘pre-finished’ materials; control the dust by using on-tool extraction using an H or M Class extraction unit and RPE* with an APF of 20.

Table 1 Controls for common high-risk tasks: for sanding plasterboard jointing, eliminate or limit the dust by using other finishes/systems and selecting boards with tapered edges to limit finishing needed; control the dust by using on-tool extraction using an H, M, or L Class extraction unit.
